content: 1. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors can significantly increase the exposure to R406, the major active metabolite of fostamatinib. This necessitates close monitoring for toxicities that may require a reduction in the fostamatinib dose. 2. Clarithromycin and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be considered. 3. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of futibatinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 4. Co-administration of futibatinib with dual P-gp and strong CYP3A inhibitors may increase the incidence or severity of futibatinib-related toxicities. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 5. Clarithromycin and gadobenate both prolong the QTc interval. Their concurrent use is contraindicated. 6. Clarithromycin increases the levels of gefitinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 7. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase the risk of adverse effects associated with gefitinib. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 8. Clarithromycin and gemifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be considered. 9. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of gentamicin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of gepirone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Their concurrent use is contraindicated. 11. Clarithromycin and gepirone both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 12. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of gilteritinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 13. If coadministration of gilteritinib with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, closely monitor for gilteritinib-related adverse effects. 14. Clarithromycin and givinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be considered. 15. If coadministration of givinostat is unavoidable, obtain ECGs at initiation, during concomitant use, and as clinically indicated. Withhold treatment if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or increases by more than 60 ms from baseline. 16. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of glasdegib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 17. Clarithromycin and glasdegib both prolong the QTc interval. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for an increased risk of QTc interval prolongation. 18. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Clarithromycin increases the levels of glimepiride, glipizide, and glyburide by plasma protein binding competition, increasing the risk of hypoglycemia. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Goserelin increases the toxicity of clarithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Clarithromycin and granisetron both prolong the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be considered. 22. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 23. Griseofulvin decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 24. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of guanfacine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 25. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors significantly increase guanfacine plasma concentrations. For extended-release guanfacine, reduce the dosage to half the recommended dose if coadministered. 26. Clarithromycin and haloperidol both prolong the QTc interval. Clarithromycin also increases the levels or effects of haloperidol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 27. Clarithromycin increases the effects of heparin by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 28. Histrelin increases the toxicity of clarithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of hydrocodone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required due to the risk of potentially fatal respiratory depression. 30. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of hydrocortisone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 31. Hydrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 32. Clarithromycin and hydroxychloroquine sulfate both prolong the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be considered. 33. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of hydroxyprogesterone caproate by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 34. Hydroxyzine increases the toxicity of clarithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Clarithromycin increases the levels of ibrutinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 36. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., anti-infectives for ≤7 days), interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued. 37. Clarithromycin and ibutilide both prolong the QTc interval. Their concurrent use is contraindicated. 38. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of idelalisib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 39. If coadministered with strong CYP3A inhibitors, monitor for signs of idelalisib toxicity and follow dosage modification recommendations if adverse reactions occur. 40. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 41. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of ifosfamide by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 42. Co-administration of CYP3A4 inhibitors may decrease the metabolism of ifosfamide to its active alkylating metabolites, reducing its efficacy. 43. Clarithromycin and iloperidone both prolong the QTc interval. Iloperidone also increases the levels of clarithromycin by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may lead to increased plasma levels of drugs predominantly eliminated by CYP3A4. 45. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of imatinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Clarithromycin and imipramine both prolong the QTc interval. Clarithromycin also increases the levels or effects of imipramine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 47. Clarithromycin increases the levels of indacaterol (inhaled) by modulating P-gp and CYP3A4 activities. Use caution and monitor closely. No dose adjustment is warranted at the 75 mcg dose. 48. Clarithromycin and indapamide both prolong the QTc interval. Their concurrent use is contraindicated. 49. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 50. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 51. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of infigratinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 52. Clarithromycin and inotuzumab both prolong the QTc interval. If coadministration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs and electrolytes before and after initiation and monitor periodically during treatment. 53. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of irinotecan and irinotecan liposomal by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 54. UGT1A1 inhibitors decrease irinotecan metabolism.
